summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after experiencing a witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure, likely due to four days of missed antiepileptic medications after leaving rehab against medical advice. He presented with hypoglycemia (glucose 44) and transient hypotension, both managed with dextrose and IV fluids. CT scans showed no acute intracranial or cervical spine abnormalities. He was loaded with IV levetiracetam and restarted on oral seizure medications, remaining seizure-free during admission. Hypotension recurred post-dialysis but resolved with cautious fluid administration. A skin swab near his femoral dialysis catheter grew staph and VRE, prompting a short course of vancomycin, though blood cultures remained negative and infection was not confirmed. An incidental enlarged thyroid with calcifications was noted on imaging; TSH was normal, and outpatient ultrasound was recommended. The patient was medically stable by discharge, alert, ambulating with a walker, and deemed competent to reside in a hotel while securing independent housing. He was discharged on updated medications with clear instructions for dialysis attendance, weight monitoring, and neurology and primary care follow-up.
